hostBackdropVariant.note: TileStyles.xaml defines a HostBackdrop-sourced acrylic; this is the variant comparable to Win32 AccentPolicy, which composites over the desktop wallpaper rather than in-window content.
hostBackdropVariant.implication: SystemControlAcrylicElementBrush uses BackgroundSource=Backdrop (in-window sampling) and is NOT the right reference for AccentPolicy tuning. The HostBackdrop values above (#101010 at 0.75 -> 0xBF101010) match what the Win10 path already uses, so both themes land on the same Win32 parameters.

unresolved.LauncherFrame_FallbackBackgroundBrush: Referenced by LauncherFrame.xaml FallbackFullBleedBackground but not defined in any StartDocked XBF; resolved at runtime outside the XAML resource set.
unresolved.StartMenuHighContrastBorderBrush: Referenced by StartSizingFrame.xaml HighContrastOuterBorder but not defined in any StartDocked XBF.
unresolved.OverlayCornerRadius: Referenced by StartSizingFrame.xaml for the root frame and drop shadow; a platform WinUI token, not defined in StartDocked.

renderedCrossCheck.finding: Rendered Start surface samples are desaturated wine-red, not the neutral #242424 declared as TintColor. Samples vary slightly across the surface, indicating live backdrop content participates in the composition.
renderedCrossCheck.conclusion: TintColor #242424 at TintOpacity 0.85 is a tint layer composited over a sampled backdrop, not the final surface color. The wallpaper on this machine is wine-red, which is why the menu reads wine-red.
renderedCrossCheck.implication: Win11 Start uses backdrop-sampling acrylic, mechanically the same family as the existing Win10 path; only the tint parameters differ. Hardcoding any single observed surface color would only match the current wallpaper and must not be done.
renderedCrossCheck.caveat: Sampled colors are specific to the wallpaper active at capture time and are evidence about the mechanism, not reusable color constants.

notes: Extracted from the live 26200.8875 machine; values are compile-time definitions, not screenshot-derived approximations.
app.xaml merges FluentResources.xaml and SharedThemeManagerBrushes.xaml at Application scope, so both dictionaries apply globally to the Start menu.
The Default theme dictionary applies on this machine: AppsUseLightTheme=0, EnableTransparency=1.
SharedThemeManagerBrushes uses x:Key Default/Light/HighContrast; FluentResources uses Light/Dark/HighContrast. Dark-mode subtle fills come from the FluentResources Dark dictionary.
The reference screenshot is cropped to the Start menu; the original full-screen capture contained unrelated browser content and was deleted rather than committed.
